circuit:Abu Dhabi.title: Yas Marina Circuit
circuit:Abu Dhabi.summary: Yas Marina Circuit, a 5. 281 km track designed by Hermann Tilke on Abu Dhabi's Yas Island, has been the home of Formula One's season finale since 2009. The venue represents the second Middle Eastern Formula One circuit, following Bahrain's establishment and preceding later additions in Qatar and Saudi Arabia.

circuit:Australia.title: Albert Park Circuit
circuit:Australia.summary: The Albert Park Circuit is a street course that winds around Albert Park Lake in Melbourne's Albert Park suburb and hosts the annual Formula One Australian Grand Prix alongside various support categories including a Supercars championship event. The venue holds the highest FIA classification for permanent racing circuits.

circuit:Austria.title: Red Bull Ring
circuit:Austria.summary: Located in Spielberg, Austria, this 4. 326 km circuit has a rich history hosting the Austrian Grand Prix across two separate periods: initially under its original name from 1970 to 1987, and again following its reconstruction and renaming from 1997 to 2003.

circuit:Azerbaijan.title: Baku City Circuit
circuit:Azerbaijan.summary: The Baku City Circuit is a street racing venue situated in Azerbaijan's capital city near the waterfront promenade, stretching 6. 003 km to rank among the longest tracks in Formula One racing. After hosting the 2016 European Grand Prix as its first F1 event, the circuit established its own championship race the following year with the Azerbaijan Grand Prix, which continues as an annual fixture on the racing calendar.

circuit:Bahrain.title: Bahrain International Circuit
circuit:Bahrain.summary: Opened in 2004, the Bahrain International Circuit is a 5. 412 km venue that hosts the annual Formula One Grand Prix, which marked the first F1 race held in the Middle East. Beyond Formula One, the track accommodates various motorsport events including endurance racing, GP2 competition, and previously hosted V8 Supercar racing, with multiple circuit configurations available for different competitions.

circuit:Barcelona.title: Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya
circuit:Barcelona.summary: Located near Barcelona in Montmeló, the Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya is a 4. 657 km track featuring a balanced mix of extended straights and diverse corner configurations that test multiple driving skills. The venue holds FIA Grade 1 certification and accommodates approximately 140,700 spectators across its facilities.

circuit:Belgium.title: Circuit de Spa-Francorchamps
circuit:Belgium.summary: The 7-kilometre Belgian circuit at Francorchamps has hosted Formula One racing since 1950, appearing on the inaugural world championship calendar. Located near the town of Spa, the venue has staged its Grand Prix annually from 1985 onwards, with only two exceptions in 2003 and 2006.

circuit:Canada.title: Circuit Gilles Villeneuve
circuit:Canada.summary: Located on Notre Dame Island in Montreal, the Circuit Gilles Villeneuve is a 4. 361-kilometre track that serves as the home of Formula One's Canadian Grand Prix. Beyond Formula One, the venue has hosted various international racing series including sports car championships, North American open-wheel competitions, and NASCAR events.

circuit:China.title: Shanghai International Circuit
circuit:China.summary: Located in Shanghai's Jiading District, the Shanghai International Circuit serves as the primary venue for the Chinese Grand Prix, which ran annually from 2004 to 2019 before resuming in 2024. The track has expanded its motorsport calendar to include electric racing events starting in 2024.

circuit:Great Britain.title: Silverstone Circuit
circuit:Great Britain.summary: Silverstone Circuit, located in England near Northamptonshire, has been the principal venue for the British Grand Prix since 1948 and notably hosted the inaugural World Championship race in 1950. After sharing the British Grand Prix with Aintree and Brands Hatch between 1955 and 1986, the circuit became the permanent home of this event from 1987 onwards, while also regularly accommodating the MotoGP series.

circuit:Hungary.title: Hungaroring
circuit:Hungary.summary: The Hungaroring, located near Budapest in Hungary, hosted the inaugural Formula One Grand Prix held behind the Iron Curtain in 1986. Built in just eight months on a site chosen by the Hungarian government over a proposed street circuit in the capital's main park, the 4. 381 km track was constructed to commemorate János Drapál, Hungary's pioneering motorcycle racer.

circuit:Italy.title: Autodromo Nazionale Monza
circuit:Italy.summary: Located near Milan in northern Italy, the Autodromo Nazionale Monza is a 5. 793 km circuit constructed in 1922 as the third purpose-built racing venue globally and Europe's oldest on mainland territory. The track, nicknamed "the Temple of Speed" for its extended straights and quick corners, has hosted the Italian Grand Prix continuously since 1949, except during a 1980 closure for renovation work.

circuit:Japan.title: Suzuka International Racing Course
circuit:Japan.summary: Suzuka Circuit is a 5. 807 km Japanese motorsport venue situated in Mie Prefecture and operated by Honda Mobilityland, featuring a 155,000-person capacity. The track serves as a prominent host for both Formula One world championship races and Japanese Super Formula competitions.

circuit:Las Vegas.title: Las Vegas Strip Circuit
circuit:Las Vegas.summary: The Las Vegas Strip Circuit is a temporary street course laid out around the famous Las Vegas Boulevard in Paradise, Nevada, weaving through sections hosting the city's premier casino resorts and hotels. The track incorporates several iconic Las Vegas landmarks such as MSG Sphere, Caesars Palace, Bellagio, and Paris Las Vegas as it navigates the urban landscape.

circuit:Mexico City.title: Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez
circuit:Mexico City.summary: Located in Mexico City, the Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez is a 4. 304 km circuit honoring brothers Ricardo and Pedro Rodríguez, both prominent racing drivers who died in accidents. The track has hosted Formula One's Mexican Grand Prix across multiple eras, resuming as a regular venue from 2015 onwards on its current layout, having previously held the event until 1992 on a different configuration.

circuit:Miami.title: Miami International Autodrome
circuit:Miami.summary: The Miami International Autodrome is a temporary street circuit constructed around Hard Rock Stadium in Miami Gardens, featuring a 3. 363-mile layout with 19 corners that generates qualifying speeds near 139 mph. Designed by Apex Circuit Design specifically for Formula One use, the track joined the championship calendar in 2022 as the venue for the Miami Grand Prix.

circuit:Monaco.title: Circuit de Monaco
circuit:Monaco.summary: The Circuit de Monaco stretches 3. 337 kilometres through the streets of Monte Carlo and La Condamine, hugging the waterfront of the principality. Though officially named after Monaco itself, the track is widely known as Monte Carlo because the majority of its layout occupies that particular neighbourhood.

circuit:Netherlands.title: Circuit Zandvoort
circuit:Netherlands.summary: Located in the Dutch coastal dunes west of Amsterdam, Zandvoort is a 4. 259 km track that hosted Formula One racing from 1958 to 1985 before its return in 2021 with the revival of the Dutch Grand Prix. The circuit will conclude its current Formula One partnership after the 2026 season.

circuit:Qatar.title: Lusail International Circuit
circuit:Qatar.summary: Lusail International Circuit is situated near Doha in Qatar and features a 5. 419-kilometer layout with a 1. 068-kilometer main straight, holding FIA Grade 1 certification.

circuit:São Paulo.title: Autódromo José Carlos Pace
circuit:São Paulo.summary: Interlagos is a 4. 309 km Brazilian motorsport facility in São Paulo that opened in 1940 and was later renamed after Formula One driver José Carlos Pace, who perished in an aviation accident in 1977. The track operates in a counterclockwise direction and features supporting amenities including a kart circuit dedicated to fellow racing legend Ayrton Senna.

circuit:Saudi Arabia.title: Jeddah Corniche Circuit
circuit:Saudi Arabia.summary: The Jeddah Corniche Circuit is a street track situated along the Red Sea waterfront in Jeddah, Saudi Arabia, serving as the venue for the Formula One Saudi Arabian Grand Prix from 2021 onwards and the Formula E championship from 2025.

circuit:Singapore.title: Marina Bay Street Circuit
circuit:Singapore.summary: The Marina Bay Street Circuit winds through Singapore's downtown waterfront area, utilizing roads around the iconic Marina Bay and spanning across the Downtown Core and Kallang districts.

circuit:Spain.title: Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya
circuit:Spain.summary: Located near Barcelona in Montmeló, Spain, the Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya spans 4. 657 kilometers and features a balanced combination of extended straights and diverse corner configurations, making it suitable for testing all aspects of racing performance. The venue holds FIA Grade 1 certification and accommodates approximately 140,700 spectators across its grandstand facilities.

circuit:United States.title: Circuit of the Americas
circuit:United States.summary: The Circuit of the Americas in Austin, Texas is a 3. 426-mile FIA Grade 1 facility that primarily hosts the Formula One United States Grand Prix alongside major NASCAR and MotoGP events. Beyond these marquee races, the venue has accommodated various international motorsport series including endurance racing championships and previously hosted IndyCar and rallycross competitions.

driver:ALB.title: Alexander Albon
driver:ALB.summary: Alexander Albon is a Thai-British motorsport competitor who represents Thailand in Formula One, currently driving for Williams.

driver:ALO.title: Fernando Alonso
driver:ALO.summary: Spanish driver Fernando Alonso competes for Aston Martin in Formula One, bringing a record of two world championship titles earned with Renault in 2005 and 2006, along with 32 Grand Prix victories accumulated over 23 seasons. Beyond single-seaters, Alonso has achieved remarkable success in endurance racing, including victories at Le Mans twice and the 2018-19 World Endurance Championship, making him the sole driver to have won both F1 and World Sportscar championships.

driver:ANT.title: Andrea Kimi Antonelli
driver:ANT.summary: Italian driver Andrea Kimi Antonelli represents Mercedes in Formula One, having claimed six race victories since entering the sport in 2025.

driver:BEA.title: Oliver Bearman
driver:BEA.summary: Oliver Bearman is a British motorsport competitor currently driving for Haas in the Formula One world championship.

driver:BOR.title: Gabriel Bortoleto
driver:BOR.summary: Brazilian driver Gabi Bortoleto currently races in Formula One as a member of the Audi team, competing at the sport's highest level.

driver:BOT.title: Valtteri Bottas
driver:BOT.summary: Finnish driver Valtteri Bottas currently races for Cadillac in Formula One, bringing extensive experience from a career spanning over a decade. He achieved runner-up finishes in the drivers' championship during consecutive seasons with Mercedes, and has accumulated 10 race victories throughout his time in the sport.

driver:COL.title: Franco Colapinto
driver:COL.summary: Franco Alejandro Colapinto is an Argentine racing driver currently competing in Formula One as part of the Alpine team.

driver:DOO.title: Jack Doohan (racing driver)
driver:DOO.summary: Jack Doohan is an Australian driver who races in the European Le Mans Series' LMP2 category with Nielsen Racing while holding a reserve driver position at Haas in Formula One. He has made seven Grand Prix appearances between 2024 and 2025.

driver:GAS.title: Pierre Gasly
driver:GAS.summary: Pierre Gasly is a French Formula One driver currently racing for Alpine. The 2020 Italian Grand Prix victory with AlphaTauri remains a significant achievement in his racing career.

driver:HAD.title: Isack Hadjar
driver:HAD.summary: A French-Algerian motorsport competitor, Isack Alexandre Hadjar represents France in Formula One while driving for Red Bull Racing.

driver:HAM.title: Lewis Hamilton
driver:HAM.summary: Lewis Hamilton is a British Formula One driver currently competing for Ferrari who has secured seven world championship titles, matching Michael Schumacher's record. He holds multiple performance records in the sport, including the most race victories, pole positions, and podium finishes in Formula One history.

driver:HUL.title: Nico Hülkenberg
driver:HUL.summary: German driver Nicolas Hülkenberg currently races for Audi in Formula One, bringing significant experience from his lengthy career in the sport. Beyond his Formula One efforts, he achieved notable success in endurance racing, including a victory at the 24 Hours of Le Mans in 2015 while driving for Porsche.

driver:LAW.title: Liam Lawson
driver:LAW.summary: Liam Lawson, a New Zealand motorsport competitor, currently drives for Racing Bulls in Formula One.

driver:LEC.title: Charles Leclerc
driver:LEC.summary: The Monégasque driver races for Ferrari in Formula One, having achieved nine Grand Prix victories throughout his career. Leclerc finished as championship runner-up in 2022 while competing for the Italian team.

driver:MAG.title: Kevin Magnussen
driver:MAG.summary: Kevin Magnussen is a Danish driver who stepped away from Formula One after 2024, having previously competed in the sport across 2014-2020 and 2022-2024. He currently focuses on endurance racing with BMW's factory team in the WEC while also pursuing a part-time NASCAR career driving for Trackhouse Racing.

driver:NOR.title: Lando Norris
driver:NOR.summary: Lando Norris is a British Formula One driver currently racing for McLaren, where he claimed the 2025 World Drivers' Championship. Throughout his eight seasons in the sport, he has secured 12 Grand Prix victories.

driver:OCO.title: Esteban Ocon
driver:OCO.summary: Esteban Ocon is a French Formula One driver currently racing for Haas. He previously secured victory at the 2021 Hungarian Grand Prix while competing for Alpine.

driver:PER.title: Sergio Pérez
driver:PER.summary: Mexican driver Sergio Pérez competes for Cadillac in Formula One, bringing extensive experience from his 15-season career in the sport. He finished as championship runner-up in 2023 while driving for Red Bull and has accumulated six Grand Prix victories throughout his time in the series.

driver:PIA.title: Oscar Piastri
driver:PIA.summary: The Australian driver Oscar Piastri currently races for McLaren in Formula One, having accumulated nine Grand Prix victories since joining the championship.

driver:RIC.title: Daniel Ricciardo
driver:RIC.summary: An Australian racing driver who participated in Formula One throughout the 2011-2024 period, Ricciardo earned the nickname "the Honey Badger" during his competitive career spanning 14 seasons. He achieved eight Grand Prix victories during his time in the sport.

driver:RUS.title: George Russell (racing driver)
driver:RUS.summary: British driver George Russell currently competes for Mercedes in Formula One, having secured seven Grand Prix victories throughout his eight-season career in the sport.

driver:SAI.title: Carlos Sainz Jr.
driver:SAI.summary: Spanish driver Carlos Sainz Vázquez de Castro currently races for Williams in Formula One, having secured four Grand Prix victories throughout his 12-season career in the sport.

driver:SAR.title: Logan Sargeant
driver:SAR.summary: American driver Logan Sargeant raced in Formula One during the 2023 and 2024 seasons before transitioning to endurance racing. He currently competes in the FIA World Endurance Championship's LMGT3 category for Proton Competition, having previously contested IMSA's LMP2 class.

driver:STR.title: Lance Stroll
driver:STR.summary: Lance Stroll is a Canadian motorsport competitor who currently races in Formula One, driving for the Aston Martin team.

driver:TSU.title: Yuki Tsunoda
driver:TSU.summary: Yuki Tsunoda, a Japanese motorsport competitor, held a reserve driver position with Red Bull Racing and Racing Bulls during his Formula One involvement spanning 2021 through 2025.

driver:VER.title: Max Verstappen
driver:VER.summary: Max Verstappen is a Dutch-Belgian driver competing for Red Bull Racing who has claimed four consecutive world championships between 2021 and 2024. The accomplished racer has secured 71 Grand Prix victories throughout his 12-season Formula One career.

driver:ZHO.title: Zhou Guanyu
driver:ZHO.summary: Zhou Guanyu is China's sole Formula One competitor to date, having raced in the championship from 2022 through 2024. He currently holds a reserve driver position with Cadillac in the series.

team:Alpine.title: Alpine F1 Team
team:Alpine.summary: Alpine Racing operates as Renault's Formula One works team from its Enstone base, competing under the French manufacturer's sports car brand since 2021 before Renault's withdrawal at the end of 2025. The team secured its only victory in this guise when Esteban Ocon triumphed at the 2021 Hungarian Grand Prix, and currently competes with Mercedes power units, a partnership previously established during its earlier Lotus incarnation.

team:Aston Martin.title: Aston Martin in Formula One
team:Aston Martin.summary: Aston Martin, a British automotive manufacturer, has maintained a presence in Formula One through different organizational structures, currently competing under the AMR GP Limited banner as the Aston Martin Aramco Formula One Team.

team:Ferrari.title: Scuderia Ferrari
team:Ferrari.summary: Scuderia Ferrari, the racing arm of the Italian luxury automaker Ferrari, is motorsport's oldest continuously competing Formula One outfit and its most accomplished, participating in every World Championship season since the sport's 1950 inception. The team's iconic emblem has earned them the popular moniker "the Prancing Horse.

team:Haas F1 Team.title: Haas F1 Team
team:Haas F1 Team.summary: Gene Haas founded this American-licensed F1 team in 2014, with the outfit making its competitive debut in 2016. Ayao Komatsu became team principal in 2024, succeeding Guenther Steiner who had led the squad since its establishment.

team:Kick Sauber.title: Sauber Motorsport
team:Kick Sauber.summary: A Swiss engineering and racing enterprise established in 1970, this constructor initially built sports cars before transitioning to Formula One machinery as an independent team. Following notable endurance racing successes including the 1989 Le Mans victory with Mercedes-Benz, the operation competed in Formula One from 1993 until 2025, becoming one of the sport's longest-serving constructors before Audi acquired its operations to establish their own Formula One project.

team:McLaren.title: McLaren
team:McLaren.summary: McLaren Racing Limited is a British Formula One outfit headquartered at the McLaren Technology Centre in Woking, Surrey. Operating as a subsidiary of the McLaren Group, the team is currently owned by Bahrain's Mumtalakat Holding Company.

team:Mercedes.title: Mercedes-AMG Petronas F1 Team
team:Mercedes.summary: Mercedes has maintained a continuous presence in Formula One since 1954, functioning variously as a constructor and power unit supplier. The current Mercedes-AMG Petronas team, based in Brackley under a German licence, became a tripartite operation in 2022 when Ineos joined Mercedes-Benz Group and Toto Wolff as equal stakeholders. The marque is traditionally associated with the "Silver Arrows" designation.

team:Racing Bulls.title: Racing Bulls
team:Racing Bulls.summary: Visa Cash App Racing Bulls is an Italian Formula One constructor competing since 2024, based in Faenza with additional facilities in Milton Keynes. Owned by Red Bull GmbH, it operates as the company's second works team alongside Red Bull Racing, sharing resources and engineering expertise across both operations.

team:RB.title: Racing Bulls
team:RB.summary: Racing Bulls is an Italian Formula One constructor that debuted in 2024 as part of Red Bull's multi-team strategy alongside Red Bull Racing. Based in Faenza with operations in Milton Keynes, the team represents Red Bull GmbH's expansion into a second constructor entry in the sport.

team:Red Bull Racing.title: Red Bull Racing
team:Red Bull Racing.summary: Oracle Red Bull Racing competes in Formula One under an Austrian license while operating from England, representing one of two F1 teams owned by Red Bull GmbH. Founded in 2005 and led by Christian Horner until 2025, the team transitioned to Laurent Mekies as team principal following Horner's departure.

team:Williams.title: Williams Racing
team:Williams.summary: Williams Grand Prix Engineering, established in 1977 by Frank Williams and Patrick Head following the collapse of Williams's previous racing venture, is a British Formula One constructor headquartered in Grove, Oxfordshire. The team will compete in 2026 under the Atlassian Williams F1 Team name.
